title: Working from home: dream or trap?

task.situation: ‘Fresh Ink’, an online magazine written by young people, is preparing an issue called ‘Tomorrow’s jobs’. Many adults now work from home on some days of the week, and the editors want to know what young readers think about it. They have invited articles on the question ‘Working from home: dream or trap?’
task.instruction: Write an article in which you:
points: describe how working from home changes people’s everyday lives
weigh up the advantages and drawbacks of working from home for employees
predict how your generation will work in the future

words.short: Give your article a title. Write around 250 words.
words.long: Give your article a title. Write around 400 words.

task.de: Ein Artikel für ein Online-Magazin junger Leute zum Thema Homeoffice. Drei Inhaltspunkte: beschreiben, wie Homeoffice den Alltag verändert; Vor- und Nachteile für Arbeitnehmer:innen abwägen; vorhersagen, wie eure Generation arbeiten wird. Den Titel wählen wir ganz zum Schluss.

meta.publication: Fresh Ink · online magazine · issue ‘Tomorrow’s jobs’

focus.label: future forms for predictions
focus.note: Marked: verb forms that make predictions, from the future word to the main verb: will / won’t + verb (will spend), will be + -ing (will be working), will have + past participle (will have disappeared) and be likely / unlikely to + verb. ‘Would’, ‘could’ and ‘might’ are not marked.

gaps.q: Who do we quote? Give our web designer a first name.
gaps.qDe: Ruft einen Vornamen für die Person, die wir zitieren. Keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen.

gaps.q: How old is the web designer?
gaps.qDe: Wie alt ist die Person? Ruft ein Alter zwischen 22 und 65.

steps.q: Which position does our article take?
steps.de: Zuerst wählt ihr die Position, nach der sich Abwägung, Vorhersage und Schluss richten.

options.label: Mostly a dream
options.teaser: Working from home gives people more freedom, as long as they set clear rules.

options.label: More of a trap
options.teaser: Working from home sounds great, but it often costs more than it gives.

steps.q: How do we open the article?
steps.de: Der erste Absatz soll Leser:innen neugierig machen und zur Frage des Artikels führen. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then finish the introduction in your own words and end with a question to the readers.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann den Einstieg mit eigenen Worten fertigschreiben und mit einer Frage an die Leser:innen enden.

options.label: Straight to the topic
options.text: Many people work at home now. It is nice for them because they have more time. They can get up later and they do not need to take the bus. But it is also bad for them. They are alone a lot and they work a lot. So is it a good thing or a bad thing? This article will tell you.
options.textLong: Many people work at home now. It is nice for them because they have more time. They can get up later and they do not need to take the bus. But it is also bad for them. They are alone a lot and they work a lot. Their boss can call them all the time. So is it a good thing or a bad thing? This article will tell you.
options.reject: Short, very basic sentences and vague words (nice, good, bad, a lot) make this sound far below B2. An introduction needs a hook and a wider range of vocabulary.
options.rejectDe: Kurze, sehr einfache Sätze und vage Wörter (nice, good, bad, a lot): Für dieses Niveau braucht es einen Hook und mehr Wortschatz.

options.label: Ask the readers
options.text: {{Have you ever seen someone answer work emails}} at the weekend or join a video call in slippers? Scenes like these are now normal. {{For some, working from home is}} pure freedom, while others feel they never really leave the office. {{So which [[will it be]]}} for our generation: dream or trap?
options.textLong: {{Have you ever seen someone answer work emails}} at the weekend or join a video call in slippers? Scenes like these are now part of normal life, and in many companies the office is half empty on Fridays. {{For some, working from home is}} pure freedom, while others feel they never really leave the office. {{So which [[will it be]]}} for our generation: dream or trap?
options.why: A question about the readers’ own experience makes the topic personal at once.

options.label: Start with a scene
options.text: {{It is ten o’clock at night. Although}} work officially ended hours ago, the laptop is still open on the kitchen table and the phone keeps buzzing. {{For millions of people, this is}} what working from home looks like. Is it the freedom everybody dreamt of, or a trap that [[will catch]] our generation too?
options.textLong: {{It is ten o’clock at night. Although}} work officially ended hours ago, the laptop is still open on the kitchen table and the phone keeps buzzing. Next to the keyboard, a plate of pasta has gone cold. {{For millions of people, this is}} what working from home looks like. Is it the freedom everybody dreamt of, or a trap that [[will catch]] our generation too?
options.why: A short scene shows the problem without explaining it. The final question opens the debate.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then finish the introduction in your own words: add one more detail of everyday life and end with a question to the readers.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann den Einstieg mit eigenen Worten fertigschreiben: ein weiteres Detail aus dem Alltag ergänzen und mit einer Frage an die Leser:innen enden.

steps.q: Content point 1: how does working from home change everyday life?
steps.de: Erster Inhaltspunkt: wie Homeoffice den Alltag verändert. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then describe in your own words how everyday life changes. Give an example of your own (you can invent it).
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann mit eigenen Worten beschreiben, wie sich der Alltag verändert. Ein eigenes, gern erfundenes Beispiel geben.

options.label: New routines
options.text: {{When the office moves into your flat,}} everyday routines change completely. The living room becomes an office, and the commute shrinks to ten steps from the bedroom. {{The catch is that}} work also creeps into the evenings: a quick look at the phone after dinner easily turns into an hour of emails.
options.textLong: {{When the office moves into your flat,}} everyday routines change completely. The living room becomes an office, and the commute shrinks to ten steps from the bedroom. Lunch comes from the kitchen instead of the canteen, and there is time to hang up the washing between two meetings. {{The catch is that}} work also creeps into the evenings: a quick look at the phone after dinner easily turns into an hour of emails. {{For better or worse, this new rhythm [[is unlikely to change]].}}
options.why: Clear topic sentence and everyday examples that every reader can picture.

options.label: A real example
options.text: {{For many employees, the working day no longer has a clear end.}} {NAME}, {AGE}, a web designer from Linz, knows this well. “I start at eight, take the dog for a walk at lunchtime and answer emails until late at night,” {{the designer explains.}} “{{On top of that,}} my desk is our dining table.”
options.textLong: {{For many employees, the working day no longer has a clear end.}} {NAME}, {AGE}, a web designer from Linz, knows this well. “I start at eight, take the dog for a walk at lunchtime and answer emails until late at night,” {{the designer explains.}} “{{On top of that,}} my desk is our dining table, so every evening the laptop has to make room for the plates. My neighbours probably think I never leave the flat.” {{Experiences like this [[are likely to become]]}} even more common in the years ahead.
options.why: A quote from a real-sounding person shows the change instead of just explaining it.

options.label: Describe everyday life
options.text: Many people work from home since the pandemic. They can cook their own lunch and wear comfortable clothes, but often their boss calls them in the evening because the company wants that they send some more informations. Some even check their emails in bed late at night. So work and free time get mixed up.
options.textLong: Many people work from home since the pandemic. They can cook their own lunch and wear comfortable clothes, but often their boss calls them in the evening because the company wants that they send some more informations. Parents help their children with homework while they join a video call, and the kitchen table becomes a desk for the whole family. Some even check their emails in bed late at night. So work and free time get mixed up.
options.reject: Three typical mistakes: ‘work from home since the pandemic’ (→ have been working), ‘wants that they send’ (→ wants them to send) and ‘informations’ (→ information, no plural).
options.rejectDe: Drei typische Fehler: since verlangt Present perfect (have been working), want that → want them to send, information hat keine Mehrzahl.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then describe in your own words how everyday life changes, with two examples of your own (you can invent them), and end with a prediction.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann mit eigenen Worten beschreiben, wie sich der Alltag verändert: zwei eigene, gern erfundene Beispiele und am Ende eine Vorhersage.

steps.q: Content point 2: what are the advantages and drawbacks?
steps.de: Zweiter Inhaltspunkt: Was bedeutet Homeoffice für Arbeitnehmer:innen? Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add one advantage and one drawback in your own words.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann einen Vorteil und einen Nachteil mit eigenen Worten ergänzen.

options.label: Time, clothes and lunch
options.text: For employees, the advantages are really great. You save time because you do not have to commute, you can wear comfortable clothes and you can plan your day the way you like. You can also cook your own lunch and spend more time with your pets. On top of that, you can take a short break whenever you want.
options.textLong: For employees, the advantages are really great. You save time because you do not have to commute, you can wear comfortable clothes and you can plan your day the way you like. You can also cook your own lunch and spend more time with your pets. On top of that, you can take a short break whenever you want. Parents can be at home when their children come back from school. Many people also say that they can concentrate better in a quiet room at home than in a busy office.
options.reject: The task says ‘weigh up the advantages AND drawbacks’. This paragraph only lists advantages, so content point 2 is only half done.
options.rejectDe: „Weigh up“ heißt Vor- UND Nachteile abwägen. Hier stehen nur Vorteile: Inhaltspunkt 2 ist nur halb erfüllt.

options.label: Weigh up both sides

map.dream: {{On the one hand, the benefits for remote workers are obvious.}} Employees save the time and money they spend commuting, and flexible hours let them work when they concentrate best. {{On the other hand, some people feel lonely}} without colleagues, and it can be hard to switch off. {{Even so,}} fixed team days [[will solve]] most of these problems.
map.pitfall: {{On the one hand, the benefits for remote workers are obvious.}} Employees save the time and money they spend commuting, and flexible hours let them work when they concentrate best. {{On the other hand, some people feel lonely}} without colleagues, and it can be hard to switch off. {{In the end,}} these drawbacks [[are likely to outweigh]] the time people save.

map.dream: {{On the one hand, the benefits for remote workers are obvious.}} Employees save the time and money they spend commuting, and flexible hours let them work when they concentrate best. Parents can take their children to school without rushing for a train. {{On the other hand, some people feel lonely}} without colleagues, and it can be hard to switch off. Promotions may also go to people who are seen in the office more often. {{Even so,}} fixed team days [[will solve]] most of these problems, and few employees [[will want]] to give up their new freedom.
map.pitfall: {{On the one hand, the benefits for remote workers are obvious.}} Employees save the time and money they spend commuting, and flexible hours let them work when they concentrate best. Parents can take their children to school without rushing for a train. {{On the other hand, some people feel lonely}} without colleagues, and it can be hard to switch off. Promotions may also go to people who are seen in the office more often. {{In the end,}} these drawbacks [[are likely to outweigh]] the time people save, and many [[will miss]] the chats at the coffee machine.

options.why: The classic structure for weighing up, with a final sentence that shows our position.

options.label: Benefits first, then the catch

map.dream: {{Still, working from home clearly}} has real benefits. Without a daily commute, employees gain time for sport or sleep. {{In addition,}} many work better in a quiet room than in an open-plan office. {{However, there is a drawback, too:}} colleagues turn into faces on a screen. {{Even so,}} few who have tried it [[will want]] to go back.
map.pitfall: {{Still, working from home clearly}} has real benefits. Without a daily commute, employees gain time for sport or sleep. {{In addition,}} many work better in a quiet room than in an open-plan office. {{However, the price is high:}} colleagues turn into faces on a screen, and the job follows you into every room. Sooner or later, many [[will miss]] the office.

map.dream: {{Still, working from home clearly}} has real benefits. Without a daily commute, employees gain time for sport or sleep, and they save money on petrol or train tickets. {{In addition,}} many work better in a quiet room than in an open-plan office. {{However, there is a drawback, too:}} colleagues turn into faces on a screen, {{and new employees in particular}} find it harder to learn from others. {{Even so,}} few who have tried it [[will want]] to go back, and most companies [[are likely to keep]] at least some home-office days.
map.pitfall: {{Still, working from home clearly}} has real benefits. Without a daily commute, employees gain time for sport or sleep, and they save money on petrol or train tickets. {{In addition,}} many work better in a quiet room than in an open-plan office. {{However, the price is high:}} colleagues turn into faces on a screen, and the job follows you into every room. {{New employees in particular}} find it harder to learn from others when the team only meets online. {{Sooner or later, many [[will miss]] the office,}} and some [[will feel]] that they have lost more than they gained.

options.why: Starts with a strong statement, then turns with ‘however’. The ending shows which side wins for us.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then add two advantages and two drawbacks in your own words and end with a prediction that shows our position.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann zwei Vorteile und zwei Nachteile mit eigenen Worten ergänzen und mit einer Vorhersage enden, die unsere Position zeigt.

steps.q: Content point 3: how will our generation work?
steps.de: Dritter Inhaltspunkt: Wie wird unsere Generation in Zukunft arbeiten? Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then write your own prediction with ‘will be working’, ‘will have changed’ or ‘is likely to’.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann eine eigene Vorhersage mit will be working, will have changed oder is likely to schreiben.

options.label: A hybrid future

map.dream: {{As for the future, I expect that by the time we are thirty,}} the classic nine-to-five job [[will have disappeared]]. {{Instead, most of us [[will work]]}} in a hybrid way, spending two or three days at home and the rest in the office. {{Thanks to fast internet,}} some [[will be answering]] emails from a beach in Greece.
map.pitfall: {{As for the future, I expect my generation [[will work]] flexibly,}} but not alone behind a screen. {{Instead, many of us [[will probably prefer]]}} co-working spaces or offices with fixed team days because we need other people. {{Furthermore, I could imagine}} a ‘right to disconnect’, as in France, becoming law in Austria.

map.dream: {{As for the future, I expect that by the time we are thirty,}} the classic nine-to-five job [[will have disappeared]]. {{Instead, most of us [[will work]]}} in a hybrid way, spending two or three days at home and the rest in the office. {{Thanks to fast internet,}} some [[will be answering]] emails from a beach in Greece. This freedom [[will also change]] where we live: if we only commute twice a week, a home in the countryside suddenly makes sense, and small villages with empty shops could come back to life.
map.pitfall: {{As for the future, I expect my generation [[will work]] flexibly,}} but not alone behind a screen. {{Instead, many of us [[will probably prefer]]}} co-working spaces or offices with fixed team days because we need other people. Such spaces could even open in small towns, so that nobody has to choose between village life and colleagues. {{Furthermore, I could imagine}} a ‘right to disconnect’, as in France, becoming law in Austria. That way, the laptop [[will stay]] closed after work, and our evenings [[will belong]] to us again.

options.why: A clear prediction with future forms, supported by concrete details.

options.label: A generation of freelancers

map.dream: {{Looking ahead, I think}} fewer of us [[will spend]] our whole career with one company. {{Instead, many [[will be working]]}} as freelancers, choosing their own projects and hours. {{Because of this, the most important skill [[will be]]}} self-management: knowing when to start, when to stop and how to stay motivated without a boss.
map.pitfall: {{Looking ahead, I think}} more and more of us [[will work]] as freelancers or gig workers. This may sound exciting, yet it also means less job security and no colleagues to share problems with. {{In such a world, the most important skill [[will be]]}} knowing where your job ends and your life begins.

map.dream: {{Looking ahead, I think}} fewer of us [[will spend]] our whole career with one company. {{Instead, many [[will be working]]}} as freelancers, choosing their own projects and hours. A translator in Graz might work for a start-up in Berlin in the morning and a client in Mexico City in the afternoon. By 2040, many of us [[will have worked]] for clients we have never met in person. {{Because of this, the most important skill [[will be]]}} self-management: knowing when to start, when to stop and how to stay motivated without a boss.
map.pitfall: {{Looking ahead, I think}} more and more of us [[will work]] as freelancers or gig workers. {{This may sound exciting, yet}} it also means less job security and no colleagues to share problems with. Freelancers usually have no paid holidays, and a week in bed with flu can mean a week without income. {{In such a world, the most important skill [[will be]]}} knowing where your job ends and your life begins. {{Many of us [[will have to save]]}} for bad months ourselves, and those who cannot say no to a client [[will end up]] working day and night.

options.why: Uses topic vocabulary such as ‘freelancer’ and shows what the change means for our generation.

options.label: Computers and robots
options.text: Meanwhile, my generation will work in many different ways. Some people, for instance, will work from home every day, while others will never work from home. Moreover, many jobs will need fast computers and good internet at home. In conclusion, robots will do a lot of jobs instead of people, especially in big factories.
options.textLong: Meanwhile, my generation will work in many different ways. Some people, for instance, will work from home every day, while others will never work from home. Moreover, many jobs will need fast computers and good internet at home. In conclusion, robots will do a lot of jobs instead of people, especially in big factories. Video calls will replace many business trips, and meetings will often take place online. Young people will also expect more free time than their parents had, and many of them will want to work four days a week.
options.reject: The linking words are used wrongly: ‘Meanwhile’ refers to nothing that happens at the same time, and ‘In conclusion’ introduces a brand-new point in the middle of a paragraph.
options.rejectDe: Die Linking words passen nicht: Meanwhile ohne gleichzeitiges Geschehen, und In conclusion leitet mitten im Absatz einen ganz neuen Punkt ein.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then write two predictions of your own with ‘will be working’, ‘will have changed’ or ‘is likely to’ and say what they mean for our lives.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann zwei eigene Vorhersagen mit will be working, will have changed oder is likely to schreiben und sagen, was sie für unser Leben bedeuten.

steps.q: How do we end the article?
steps.de: Der Schluss rundet den Artikel ab. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then sum up our view in two or three sentences of your own.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann unsere Sicht in zwei bis drei eigenen Sätzen zusammenfassen.

options.label: Sum up

map.dream: {{All in all, working from home is}} more dream than trap, as long as we stay in control of it. The laptop [[is likely to stay]] in our homes, but it should not take over our free time. {{So, are you ready for}} the office of the future?
map.pitfall: {{All in all, working from home is}} a dream that can quickly turn into a trap. Freedom without limits is not really freedom, and our generation [[will have to learn]] where to draw the line. {{So, are you ready for}} that challenge?

map.dream: {{All in all, working from home is}} more dream than trap, as long as we stay in control of it. It saves time and gives us more freedom over our day. {{The laptop [[is likely to stay]] in our homes,}} and our generation [[will have to make]] sure that it does not take over our free time. {{So, are you ready for}} the office of the future?
map.pitfall: {{All in all, working from home is}} a dream that can quickly turn into a trap. The time we save on the commute is easily lost again in long evenings at the laptop, and a screen [[will never replace]] a team. {{Freedom without limits is not really freedom,}} and our generation [[will have to learn]] where to draw the line. {{So, are you ready for}} that challenge?

options.why: Sums up our position in one sentence and ends with a question to the readers.

options.label: Turn to the readers

map.dream: {{Next time you hear someone complain about working from home,}} think of the time and freedom it gives. Used wisely, it [[is likely to make]] our generation’s working lives healthier, not more stressful. {{After all,}} who would not want to skip the morning rush hour?
map.pitfall: {{Next time your laptop calls you at nine in the evening, ask yourself:}} who is in charge here, you or your job? Without clear limits, the dream [[will soon turn]] into a trap. {{After all,}} a home should be a place to rest, not a second office.

map.dream: {{Next time you hear someone complain about working from home,}} think of the time and freedom it gives, from an extra hour of sleep to lunch with the family. {{Its dangers are real, but}} our generation [[will learn]] to manage them. Used wisely, it [[is likely to make]] our working lives healthier, not more stressful. {{After all,}} who would not want to skip the morning rush hour?
map.pitfall: {{Next time your laptop calls you at nine in the evening, ask yourself:}} who is in charge here, you or your job? The time saved on the commute is worth little if work fills every room and every evening. Without clear limits, the dream [[will soon turn]] into a trap. {{After all,}} a home should be a place to rest, not a second office.

options.why: Speaks to readers directly and leaves them with something to think about.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then sum up our view in three or four sentences of your own: everyday life, advantages and drawbacks, the future.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann unsere Sicht in drei bis vier eigenen Sätzen zusammenfassen: Alltag, Vor- und Nachteile, Zukunft.

steps.q: Now that the article is finished, which title do we choose?
steps.de: Zuletzt wählen wir den Titel für unseren Artikel.
steps.own: Catchy and short: a play on words, a question or a surprising statement that fits our article.
steps.ownDe: Kurz und packend: ein Wortspiel, eine Frage oder eine überraschende Aussage, passend zu unserem Artikel.

options.label: A play on words
options.why: Plays on the saying ‘Home sweet home’. The question mark shows that it might not be so sweet.

options.label: A twist on an old phrase
options.why: Contrasts the old nine-to-five job with the new way of working in just a few words.

options.label: A slogan for our position
options.why: Sums up our position in a short, catchy phrase.

checks.en: A catchy title, ideally a play on words or a question
An introduction with a hook that ends with a question
All three content points: everyday life, advantages and drawbacks, a prediction
Five paragraphs; each body paragraph opens with a topic sentence linked to what came before
Future forms for predictions (will, will be working, will have changed, is likely to)
Linking words that show the real logic (contrast, reason, result)
Readers are addressed directly; neutral to semi-informal register, no slang

teacher.aim: Die Klasse baut gemeinsam einen Artikel nach SRDP-Standard zum Thema Homeoffice und übt dabei, Vor- und Nachteile abzuwägen und eine begründete Vorhersage zu treffen. Fokus: Zukunftsformen für Vorhersagen – will, will be working (Future progressive), will have changed (Future perfect) und be likely to.
teacher.prep: A/B/C/D-Karten austeilen, eine Garnitur pro Person (ohne Karten: 1–4 Finger, die Tasten 1–4 wählen wie A–D). Beamer im Vollbild. Die Aufgabe am Beamer enthält alles Nötige. Im Gerüst-Modus den eingebauten Timer nutzen: 5–6 min pro Absatz.
teacher.heft: Neue Seite: Datum (rechts), „Article“ als Überschrift, darunter 2 Zeilen für den Titel frei lassen (der Titel kommt zuletzt). Fünf Absätze, jeder beginnt nach einer Leerzeile; am Rand stehen Intro, Body 1, Body 2, Body 3 und Conclusion. Zukunftsformen grün unterstreichen.
teacher.flow: 7 Entscheidungen (Position, Einleitung, Body 1–3, Schluss, Titel). Volltext kurz (50 min): 3 min Aufgabe lesen und Position wählen, 6 weitere Entscheidungen à ca. 2 min, Abschreiben ca. 25 min, 5 min Checkliste. Volltext lang (100 min): dieselben 7 Entscheidungen, aber längere Absätze: vor jeder Abstimmung 2 min Lesezeit für die langen Karten, Abschreiben ca. 40 min, am Ende 10 min Wortzahl, Zukunftsformen und Checkliste. Gerüst kurz (60 min): 3 min Aufgabe und Position, pro Absatz 1 min Entscheidung, 5–6 min eigenes Schreiben, 1 min Vergleich mit dem Modell; am Ende 2 min Titel und 4 min Checkliste. In 50 Minuten: Schluss und Titel als Hausübung. Gerüst lang (100 min): dieselben Entscheidungen, pro Absatz 2 min Lesen und Abstimmen, eigenes Schreiben 7–8 min bei Einleitung und Schluss, 11–12 min bei Body 1–3, je 2 min Vergleich; am Ende 2 min Titel und 4 min Checkliste. Vor Body 3 kurz an die Tafel: will be working (Vorgang in der Zukunft), will have changed (bis zu einem Zeitpunkt abgeschlossen), is likely to (wahrscheinlich).
teacher.traps: Introduction A (LSR): kurze Basissätze und vage Wörter (nice, good, bad, a lot). Body 1 C (LSA): since + Present simple statt Present perfect, want that statt want sb to do, informations. Body 2 A (TA): nur Vorteile, keine Nachteile. Body 3 C (CC): Linking words passen nicht zur Logik (Meanwhile ohne Gleichzeitigkeit, In conclusion mitten im Absatz vor einem neuen Punkt). Die Fallen haben in beiden Längen denselben Fehler. Kürzel: TA = Erfüllung der Aufgabenstellung, CC = Kohärenz und Kohäsion, LSR = Spektrum sprachlicher Mittel, LSA = Sprachrichtigkeit.
teacher.notes: Sensibel: keine Fragen zur Arbeitssituation der eigenen Eltern stellen; das Beispiel bleibt allgemein. Für den Namen in Body 1 (Option B) nur erfundene Namen, keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen. Der Artikel hat in beiden Längen genau fünf Absätze. Die lange Fassung hat dieselben Entscheidungen; jede Karte ist derselbe Absatz, nur ausführlicher (Einleitung und Schluss ca. 65 Wörter, Body 1–3 ca. 90–100). Die Position im ersten Schritt steuert das Ende von Body 2, die Vorhersage, den Schluss und einen der Titel. Markiert sind nur Zukunftsformen, die etwas vorhersagen; would, could und might bleiben unmarkiert (gut für ein kurzes Gespräch über Sicherheitsgrade). Differenzierung: Schnelle schreiben im Gerüst-Modus zu Body 3 eine zweite Vorhersage mit „By 2040, … will have …“. Hausübung: zweite Fassung mit der anderen Position.
